key_insight: Microscopic impurities nucleate perovskite degradation, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can detect and quantify them within seconds.
engineering_relevance: Rapid, non-invasive impurity screening could help manufacturers flag instability-prone wide-bandgap perovskite films before device fabrication.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation initiation.
Apply machine learning-supported analysis to reflected-light images for impurity quantification and degradation tracking.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation initiating at impurity–perovskite interfaces, while films with higher impurity density exhibited faster early degradation.
watch_item: The abstract does not report detection accuracy or validation across manufacturing conditions, leaving production-scale robustness uncertain.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
